data.name: Super Trashforce
data.detailed_description:
The near future. The world is full of radwaste. Garbage and chemicals flooded even hell. Satan became angry and sent his devilish creatures to the earth to destroy people! Because of this, even the ancient secret civilization of reptilians decided to wipe mankind from the face of the earth by entering the big war.
But brave and mostly crazy defenders of the Earth organized a special squad. It was called Super Trashforce!

Game features:
  • - 18 unique parody characters with different characteristics;
  • - 5 different levels with unique enemies for each one;
  • - Over 20 unique random bosses;
  • - More than 44 weapons. All unexpected and crazy: from a old good shotgun to rotten fish or self-guided dildos! By the way, how about a nuclear bomb?
  • - Funny voice overs;
  • - Unbelievable gore effects and black humor!

4 game modes:
  • 1) Normal Game - classic survival. Here you can earn gold skulls for open new characters;
  • 2) Boss Survival - survival for very bad dudes, because here only bosses;
  • 3) Last stand - tower defense with base, upgrade, buy soldiers and weapons;
  • 4) Conquest - strategy mode. This is a real challenge for experienced players. Capture the regions, send troops, earn prestige and open Super bosses - Ancient guards. This is really tough guys! After this final battle is waiting for you... We promise, it will be difficult, but interesting!

data.short_description: The near future. The world was flooded with waste from factories. Over time, almost all the land is bogged down in the waste. All garbage and chemicals were able to reach even to hell itself. Satan did not like it very much and he sent his creations to the ground in order to destroy all people for this garbage.

reviews.review:
Super Trashforce is a frantic top-down shooter that embraces crude humor, exaggerated violence, ridiculous weaponry, and a deliberately chaotic approach to arcade action. Developed by Crystal Box Team and published by Conglomerate 5, it presents a bizarre apocalypse in which pollution and industrial waste have become so severe that even hell has been affected. Demonic forces consequently invade Earth, while an ancient reptilian civilization joins the destruction. Humanity's response is the Super Trashforce, an unlikely collection of fighters tasked with surviving the resulting madness.

Combat is the centerpiece of the experience, with players facing increasingly dangerous groups of enemies from a traditional overhead perspective. The controls and general structure are straightforward enough to understand quickly, allowing the game to focus on constant movement, shooting, survival, and experimentation. Rather than providing only one protagonist, it features 18 playable characters with different characteristics. Unlocking additional fighters gives progression some purpose and encourages players to experiment with alternatives instead of relying on the same character for every run.

The weapon selection is one of the game's most entertaining features. More than 44 weapons are available, ranging from recognizable firearms to intentionally ridiculous choices that perfectly complement the game's sense of humor. Shotguns and other conventional weapons share space with absurd improvised equipment such as rotten fish, while extremely destructive options push the action even further into cartoonish excess. The variety helps keep combat unpredictable, especially when combined with randomized encounters and the game's fondness for throwing large quantities of enemies at the player.

Its standard survival-oriented mode serves as the foundation of the experience. Players fight through enemies, collect gold skulls, and gradually gain access to additional characters. There are five principal levels featuring their own opponents, so environments and enemy combinations change as players progress. More than 20 random bosses provide another layer of unpredictability. These bosses are particularly important because they prevent repeated attempts from following exactly the same pattern and can force players to adapt their tactics and available equipment.

Several additional modes expand the concept beyond straightforward survival. Boss Survival concentrates on encounters against powerful bosses and is better suited to players interested in testing their combat skills without spending as much time fighting ordinary enemies. Last Stand introduces tower-defense elements by asking players to protect a base while purchasing weapons, soldiers, and improvements. It provides a noticeably different rhythm because survival depends not only on personal combat ability but also on making sensible defensive investments.

Conquest is perhaps the most unusual alternative mode because it incorporates broader strategy mechanics. Players capture regions, deploy troops, accumulate prestige, and eventually encounter especially dangerous Ancient Guards. It does not suddenly transform Super Trashforce into a deep grand-strategy experience, but it demonstrates how willing the game is to experiment beyond its basic shooter framework. Having survival, boss-focused combat, defensive gameplay, and territorial conquest available in one package gives the game considerably more variety than its modest presentation initially suggests.

The audiovisual direction fully commits to the same outrageous personality. Gore is intentionally excessive, characters and situations lean into parody, and humorous voiceovers reinforce the game's refusal to take its apocalypse seriously. This style will inevitably be divisive. Players who appreciate intentionally tasteless humor, old-school arcade violence, and low-budget B-movie absurdity may find it charming, while anyone expecting sophisticated comedy or a serious atmosphere will probably struggle to connect with it.

Its greatest weakness is that the abundance of ideas is not matched by the same degree of refinement. Combat can become repetitive despite the weapon selection, and the individual modes generally offer more novelty than mechanical depth. The limited number of primary levels also means repeated play eventually exposes familiar environments and situations. Super Trashforce is consequently better suited to shorter bursts of chaotic entertainment than extremely long sessions. Its progression systems, randomized bosses, unlockable characters, multiple modes, and Steam achievements nevertheless provide enough incentives to return.

Steam Deck compatibility is not officially rated by Valve, so the game should be regarded as Unknown or Unverified for Steam Deck rather than officially Verified or Playable. Its lightweight technical requirements suggest that raw performance should not be particularly demanding, but that should not be confused with an official compatibility rating. Control behavior, interface usability, Proton compatibility, and other handheld-specific details may still require individual testing.

Overall, Super Trashforce is an eccentric action game that prioritizes variety, absurdity, and immediate entertainment over polish or sophistication. Its collection of 18 characters, more than 44 weapons, randomized bosses, multiple gameplay modes, and intentionally outrageous presentation gives it a distinctive identity. The mechanics may not have enough depth to sustain everyone over the long term, but players who enjoy chaotic top-down shooters and deliberately ridiculous humor can find a surprisingly substantial arcade experience underneath its rough exterior. 

Rating: 5/10
